headline: Heavy rain looms: Short-term flooding forecast for Chattogram region
summary: The Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre warns of rapid water level rises in several rivers across south-eastern Bangladesh.
details: The Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) has forecast short-term flooding in low-lying riverside areas of the Chattogram region due to heavy rainfall.
Heavy rain is expected in south-eastern Bangladesh, India's Tripura, and areas bordering Myanmar through July 9.
Upstream areas adjacent to south-eastern Bangladesh could receive between 300mm and 500mm of rainfall during this period.
Water levels in the Sangu, Matamuhuri, Halda, Muhuri, Feni, Selonia, and Gomti rivers in the Chattogram Division may rise rapidly.
Short-term flooding may occur in parts of Bandarban, Cox's Bazar, Chattogram, Feni, Khagrachhari, and Rangamati from July 6 to July 9.
Additionally, the Brahmaputra-Jamuna river system could reach danger levels in Kurigram, Gaibandha, Jamalpur, and Bogura between July 4 and July 7.

headline_marked: Govt to [[revise 2006 Visa Policy]] to attract investment and tourism
headline: Govt to revise 2006 Visa Policy to attract investment and tourism
summary: A cabinet committee has been formed to review the draft of 'Visa Policy 2026', aiming to make entry and exit for foreigners easier and more service-oriented.
details: The government has formed a cabinet committee, headed by Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, to review and revise the draft of the proposed 'Visa Policy 2026'.
The move is part of an initiative to update the existing visa policy, which was introduced in 2006, to make the entry and exit of foreigners easier, more orderly, and service-oriented.
The proposed policy aims to modernize the country's immigration framework and make visa services more efficient, focusing on attracting foreign investment, business, and skilled human resources.
Additionally, the policy will seek to promote tourism and the hospitality sector, facilitate technology and knowledge transfer, and manage international travel based on reciprocity.
Prime Minister's Office sources say the 2006 policy is outdated as the nature of international travel, investment, and technological cooperation has changed significantly over two decades.
Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani stated that the new policy will reduce delays in issuing visas, making it faster and easier for foreigners to enter the country to boost investment.
The home ministry will handle security issues, while the tourism and commerce ministries will provide input to enrich the policy before it is finalized.
caption:
Bangladesh is updating its 20-year-old visa policy to make it faster and easier for foreigners to enter.

The government has formed a cabinet committee, headed by Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, to review and revise the draft of the proposed 'Visa Policy 2026'.

The move is part of an initiative to update the existing visa policy, which was introduced in 2006, to make the entry and exit of foreigners easier, more orderly, and service-oriented.

The proposed policy aims to modernize the country's immigration framework and make visa services more efficient, focusing on attracting foreign investment, business, and skilled human resources.

Additionally, the policy will seek to promote tourism and the hospitality sector, facilitate technology and knowledge transfer, and manage international travel based on reciprocity.

Prime Minister's Office sources say the 2006 policy is outdated as the nature of international travel, investment, and technological cooperation has changed significantly over two decades.

Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani stated that the new policy will reduce delays in issuing visas, making it faster and easier for foreigners to enter the country to boost investment.

The home ministry will handle security issues, while the tourism and commerce ministries will provide input to enrich the policy before it is finalized.
